html:
The Hejaz is the western coast and mountains of Arabia along the Red Sea, home to the holy cities of Mecca and Medina and the port of Jeddah. On the map it appears in 600 and 700, and again from 1920 to 1938.

In 600 it was a land of trading towns and tribes, where Muhammad preached Islam in Mecca and made the Hijra to Medina in 622. By 700 it was part of the Umayyad Caliphate. For centuries afterwards, local sharifs, descendants of the Prophet, ruled Mecca under the protection of whoever ruled Egypt, and from 1517 the Ottomans.

The Ottomans built the Hejaz Railway to Medina, opened in 1908. In 1916 the Sharif of Mecca, Hussein bin Ali, led the Arab Revolt against them with British support and made himself king of the Hejaz. In 1924 and 1925 Ibn Saud of Najd conquered it. It was joined with Najd and in 1932 became part of Saudi Arabia.
